claims.statement: Open SWE's backend is a LangGraph application that serves six graphs (agent, reviewer, analyzer, review-scout, chat, scheduler) together with a FastAPI app (openswe.webapp:app); langgraph.json declares the .env env file and checkpoint deletion TTL policy.

make dev checks port 2024, starts local PostgreSQL when POSTGRES_URI is absent, and runs `uv run langgraph dev --no-browser --port 2024 --n-jobs-per-worker 10`; the full runtime serves graphs and FastAPI together on :2024.
make run runs `uvicorn openswe.webapp:app --reload --port 8000` without the LangGraph runtime, so features that create runs require make dev instead.
make install installs backend dependencies including dev extras via `uv sync --extra dev`, and Makefile wrappers run pytest, Ruff, and `ty check openswe tests`.

The local/runtime dependency constraints target langgraph-api >=0.15.0rc1,<0.16 and langgraph-runtime-inmem >=0.35.0rc1,<0.36, matching langgraph.json's 0.15 release-candidate API line and the 0.15.1 Python 3.14 Docker base.

langgraph.desktop.json is a separate trimmed deployment manifest for the desktop build: it exposes only the agent graph, uses local auth and checkpoint handlers, disables Studio auth, and disables the built-in UI.
The pnpm workspace includes bridge-client, ui, desktop, cli, and tests/e2e, while Turborepo orchestrates dev, build, typecheck, test, and check tasks.
make web runs `pnpm run dev`, which invokes Turbo only for open-swe-dashboard; its Vite development proxy targets DASHBOARD_API_URL and defaults to http://localhost:2024.
Root dashboard build, typecheck, test, and check scripts fan out through Turborepo, whereas lint (oxlint) and format/format:check (oxfmt) run directly at the repository root.
Turborepo's build task caches .output/**, .vercel/output/**, and build/** and treats DASHBOARD_API_URL, SOURCE_COMMIT, VERCEL, E2E_HARNESS, and VITE_* as cache-affecting build inputs.

The experimental Electron desktop app bundles the compiled dashboard UI, uses a selected backend URL with no maintainer-hosted default, and supports This Mac work through a local bridge that long-polls the backend for execution and file requests.

make install-desktop refuses a dirty working tree, switches and fast-forwards main, then invokes scripts/install_desktop.sh, while make install-checkout runs that script against the current checkout without changing git state.

scripts/install_desktop.sh is macOS-only, verifies Node, ditto, uv, Bun, and a pnpm/Corepack launcher, performs a frozen workspace install and desktop pack, then stages and swaps the app into /Applications or ~/Applications.

scripts/create_sandbox_snapshot.py creates a LangSmith sandbox snapshot through SandboxClient using configurable name, Docker image, filesystem capacity, and API key, then prints the resulting snapshot ID.

scripts/purge_wakeup_crons.py is a one-time backfill that can dry-run or delete expired one-shot thread_wakeup crons, resolving the deployment URL from --url/LANGGRAPH_URL and credentials from LANGGRAPH_API_KEY or LANGSMITH_API_KEY.

The root Dockerfile builds the standalone production LangGraph API server image, not a sandbox image, from langchain/langgraph-api:0.15.1-py3.14; it installs the repository, registers six graphs, the openswe.webapp FastAPI app, the TTL policy, and exposes port 8000.

A standalone backend needs DATABASE_URI, REDIS_URI, LANGSMITH_API_KEY, LANGGRAPH_CLOUD_LICENSE_KEY, and a public LANGGRAPH_URL; it must not run on scale-to-zero infrastructure because background runs rely on Redis- and Postgres-backed workers remaining available.

ui/Dockerfile is a multi-stage Node 24 Alpine build run from the repository root: it uses a frozen filtered pnpm install, builds open-swe-dashboard into a Nitro .output server, runs it as node on port 8080, and expects DASHBOARD_API_URL at runtime.

In a separate dashboard deployment, Nitro proxies browser dashboard API and webhook traffic to DASHBOARD_API_URL and server rendering forwards the osw_session cookie; same-origin use sets backend dashboard URLs and the GitHub callback to the frontend origin, while a VITE_DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL alternative requires DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

LangGraph Platform can deploy the repository directly; langgraph.json bundles a dashboard for the mount prefix as a best-effort image-build step, continuing backend deployment when the dashboard build fails.

The production Nitro proxy requires DASHBOARD_API_URL for every request and throws when it is unset; it preserves path/query, streamed non-GET bodies, separate Set-Cookie headers, and OAuth redirects while filtering invalid hop-by-hop/framing headers.

The FastAPI app rejects wildcard DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS because credentialed CORS is enabled, includes the Electron open-swe://app origin, and installs dashboard, plan, workflow, webhook, health, sandbox, and UI routes.

The backend serves a dashboard from DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR or ui/.output/public, or proxies a configured Vite dev server; its UI catch-all declines reserved API and LangGraph paths, serves a shell only to HTML navigations, and gives hashed assets immutable caching.

Dashboard assets and client-router paths must be built with DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH equal to the LangGraph http.mount_prefix; the platform manifest derives it during the dashboard build, while local prefixed builds must supply it.

make tunnel requires NGROK_DOMAIN and exposes local port 2024 through an ngrok policy that returns 404 for every path outside /webhooks/*, keeping unauthenticated LangGraph development routes private.

The root Docker image does not build the dashboard, so standalone Docker serving requires a prebuilt dashboard or DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR; the LangGraph Platform manifest instead attempts a dashboard build and continues if it fails.

A standalone backend using LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop exposes raw LangGraph routes to network clients; deployments should use LangSmith authentication or an authenticated/private network boundary because dashboard sessions and webhook signatures protect only custom routes.
make swagger generates the checked-in swagger.json from openswe.webapp:app; the generated schema covers custom FastAPI routes but not LangGraph runtime routes.
The local Compose service uses postgres:16 on loopback port 5433, waits for pg_isready, and persists its data in the named open-swe-postgres volume.

make cli uses Bun to compile cli/dist/oswe as a single executable with its runtime included; the CLI long-polls a remote deployment to execute agent-requested commands and file transfers in the invoking user's local checkout, where commands are unsandboxed.
